summaries.name: Johns Hopkins University
summaries.summary: The user completed a Data Science specialization from Johns Hopkins University before pursuing further machine learning study.

summaries.name: Udacity
summaries.summary: Udacity offers a "YOLO for Autonomous Driving" tutorial and an "Autonomous Vehicle Object Detection using YOLO" video, covering pedestrian, car, and traffic light detection.

summaries.name: Kaggle
summaries.summary: Kaggle is a platform for participating in machine learning and computer vision competitions and practicing with real-world datasets.

summaries.name: TensorFlow
summaries.summary: TensorFlow is a machine learning framework with built-in support for computer vision tasks, official tutorials, a TensorFlow Object Detection API, and a TensorFlow-based YOLO implementation used for autonomous vehicle and pedestrian object detection.

summaries.name: PyTorch
summaries.summary: PyTorch is a machine learning framework with built-in support for computer vision tasks and official tutorials; PyTorchvision is its framework for computer vision tasks including object detection and segmentation.

summaries.name: Machine Learning Mastery
summaries.summary: Machine Learning Mastery is a blog with practical ML/AI tutorials, including a YOLOv3 tutorial, and articles on using YOLO for autonomous vehicle and pedestrian detection.

summaries.name: AI Alignment
summaries.summary: AI Alignment is a podcast exploring the latest developments in AI research.

summaries.name: Towards Data Science
summaries.summary: Towards Data Science is a Medium publication featuring articles on machine learning, AI, and data science.

summaries.name: Machine Learning Subreddit
summaries.summary: The Machine Learning Subreddit is an online community of machine learning enthusiasts, researchers, and practitioners.

summaries.name: PyImageSearch
summaries.summary: PyImageSearch is a blog with in-depth computer vision tutorials using Python and OpenCV, including tutorials on YOLO, YOLOv3, SSD object detection, and Adrian Rosebrock's computer vision tutorials.

summaries.name: IEEE Transactions on Pattern Analysis and Machine Intelligence (TPAMI)
summaries.summary: IEEE Transactions on Pattern Analysis and Machine Intelligence (TPAMI) is a leading journal in computer vision and pattern recognition.

summaries.name: ImageNet
summaries.summary: ImageNet is a large-scale image dataset used for object recognition and classification.

summaries.name: CIFAR-10
summaries.summary: CIFAR-10 is a popular dataset used for image classification and object recognition.

summaries.name: Open Images Dataset
summaries.summary: The Open Images Dataset is a large-scale dataset used for object detection and segmentation.

summaries.name: PASCAL VOC
summaries.summary: PASCAL VOC is a dataset for object detection and segmentation containing 20 object classes.

summaries.name: COCO (Common Objects in Context)
summaries.summary: COCO (Common Objects in Context) is a dataset for object detection, segmentation, and captioning containing 80 object classes.

summaries.name: KITTI Object Detection Benchmark
summaries.summary: The KITTI Object Detection Benchmark is a dataset for object detection in autonomous driving scenarios, covering pedestrian, car, and traffic light detection.

summaries.name: Caltech Pedestrian Dataset
summaries.summary: The Caltech Pedestrian Dataset is used for pedestrian detection in autonomous driving scenarios.

summaries.name: Cityscapes Dataset
summaries.summary: The Cityscapes Dataset is used for semantic segmentation and object detection in urban scenarios, including pedestrian detection.

summaries.name: Argoverse Dataset
summaries.summary: The Argoverse Dataset is used for object detection and tracking in autonomous driving scenarios.

summaries.name: OpenCV
summaries.summary: OpenCV is a computer vision library with Python, C++, and Java interfaces, with built-in support for object detection and segmentation; used in the PyYOLO implementation and pedestrian detection tutorials.

summaries.name: Keras
summaries.summary: Keras is a deep learning framework with built-in support for computer vision tasks, used in the Keras-YOLO implementation.

summaries.name: TensorFlow Object Detection API
summaries.summary: The TensorFlow Object Detection API is a TensorFlow-based framework for object detection and segmentation.

summaries.name: PyTorchvision
summaries.summary: PyTorchvision is a PyTorch-based framework for computer vision tasks, including object detection and segmentation.

summaries.name: Keras Applications
summaries.summary: Keras Applications is a Keras-based framework for computer vision tasks, including object detection and segmentation.

summaries.name: SSD (Single Shot Detector)
summaries.summary: SSD (Single Shot Detector) is a fast and accurate object detection system, described in its original research paper.

summaries.name: Faster R-CNN
summaries.summary: Faster R-CNN is a fast and accurate object detection system, described in its original research paper.

summaries.name: 3Blue1Brown
summaries.summary: 3Blue1Brown is a YouTube channel with a video explaining the basics of YOLO.

summaries.name: Sentdex
summaries.summary: Sentdex is a YouTube channel with a video tutorial on implementing YOLO using Python and OpenCV.

summaries.name: Stanford CS231n
summaries.summary: Stanford CS231n is a Stanford course featuring lectures on object detection using YOLO, including applications to autonomous vehicles and pedestrian detection.
